$schema_note: Hand-curated record of what ForgePact's boss soul pieces (ForgePact#197) rely on, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/soul_piece_model.py never reads it; tests/test_soul_piece_model.py reads both, checks the shared `cases` against its own transforms of ForgePact's code, and (ParityTests, where ForgePact is checked out) pins ForgePact/plugin/include/ForgePact/SoulPieceMod.hpp's constants, seeds, act table, room rules and verdict words to this file. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/soul-piece-spec.md; the game facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21 and § 18.4; the act of each room is hs-game-sdk/curated/room_acts.json. A `status` is one of `static_reading` (read from the compiled game and paraphrased, no script text), `inference` (follows from static readings, not read directly), `owner_named` (the owner's decision, not a reading), `our_code` (ForgePact's own choice), `measured`, `unverified` (a plausible value no session has read) or `pending` (a live check of ForgePact#197 fills it). A `source` is `<path> § <section>`, the path relative to the hub root and the section text appearing in that file. `seed_base` + act is a piece's seed `a`; `reserved_seeds` are other ForgePact items' seeds a piece must never take. `gem` is the Gem of Incarnation whose `droprate.base` G ForgePact reads at run time by repository name; `ratio` makes the piece's denominator D = max(1, floor(G x numerator / denominator)), 0 (no piece) for G unknown, zero or negative. `acts` is one row per act: the boss object (an hs_game_sdk object name, with the SDK's index), the piece's name, `named` (false would make the act drop and summon nothing) and the row's evidence. `room_rules` are the name rules that refuse a room on top of the act table, each with the verdict word it gives. `drop_verdicts` and `use_verdicts` are the words, in the order ForgePact asks them; `force_overrides` the drop verdicts `soulpiece force on` may replace with `hit`. `cases` are shared inputs and their expected answer: `drop` (DecideDrop), `use` (DecideUse) and `stack` (VetoStack, consulted only after the game answered that two items stack); a roll is uniform in [0, 1). `open_questions` name the model's HYPOTHESES key each live check answers.

gem.rate_note: Info key "31" carried 10,000 on every Gem of Incarnation in the local drop records (measured), and measured gem bases are 9,000 and 11,000 (§ 13.2), so 10,000 is the plausible droprate.base; Live procedure 1's gem-rate reads it.

ratio.note: The owner, 2026-10-11: a fixed chance, a little more common than the Gem of Incarnation. D = floor(G x 4 / 5), so on the same DropGems call a piece is five quarters as likely as the gem.
